what_it_does: Chip designers use SAT solvers (satisfiability checkers—algorithms that determine if a logical formula can be true) to verify circuits are correct and find design bugs. However, standard SAT solvers convert circuits into CNF (conjunctive normal form—a generic logical formula) which erases the circuit structure that could speed up solving. This paper proposes preprocessing circuits using advanced logic synthesis techniques (simplification and restructuring rules used during chip design) combined with reinforcement learning. An RL agent learns which transformations (like converting logic to look-up table form) are most effective for a given problem, tuning the preprocessing strategy on-the-fly to minimize solver runtime. The approach treats SAT solving as a learned optimization problem rather than a generic algorithm.
